A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaRank research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable matching across reordering and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original vision and language model-merging experiments, component-loss analyses, and ablations in Sections 3 and 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds comparator results, adaptation-data sensitivity experiments, and further analyses of singular-component interference.

M1.justification: The binary component masks, entropy objective, STE optimization, and final merging procedure remain unchanged. v3 applies AdaRank to Iso-CTS and consolidates the appendix pseudocode, but documents no new pruning or optimization operation.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 8-, 14-, and 20-task vision groups and seven GLUE tasks. The added language-model loss analyses use retained coverage; varying adaptation-data amounts changes sample availability within existing datasets.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds Iso-CTS and Iso-CTS+AdaMerging comparisons alongside Iso-CTS+AdaRank. Table 2 adds TSV-M+AdaMerging and CART+AdaMerging for both language backbones, absent from v2's corresponding main and appendix comparisons. These extend existing comparator families; renaming AdaMerging to TA+AdaMerging is not a separate addition.

E3.justification: New Tables 7 and 10 vary TTA data availability across 1%, 5%, 10%, 50%, and 100%, with no-TTA and full-data AdaMerging references. Appendix C.1 adds scaled-versus-normalized component controls and paired-component sweeps. These are targeted new protocols; previously stated benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained oracle, mask, and rank ablations, v3 adds data-availability sensitivity studies in both modalities and substantially expands mechanism analysis. Figures 6-9 examine language-model component losses, spectral magnitude versus direction, Hessian curvature, and interactions between two components.

E5.justification: Reporting remains point estimates and loss plots. Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v3 introduces no new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Previously reported benchmark scores are retained, while v3 adds substantial comparator, data-sensitivity, and mechanism results. New entries include 95.5% for Iso-CTS+AdaRank on eight-task ViT-L/14. Some additions have unresolved setting inconsistencies: Table 7 labels 82.1% as eight-task CART+AdaRank with 100% data, whereas Table 1 reports 89.2%; this does not establish a same-setting performance decline.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 adds second-order Taylor expansions for single and paired component additions and a definition isolating joint-interaction loss (Equations 7-9). This supplies local mathematical reasoning for the interference analysis while retaining the existing merging equations and optimization objective.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: adaptive singular-component selection mitigates interference, accommodates task/layer rank variation, and improves merging across architectures and modalities without inference-time parameter overhead.

C2.justification: v2 discusses task similarity and conjectures benefits from bottom components. v3 substantially develops this interpretation: singular-value scaling amplifies broadly distributed misaligned directions, first-order effects dominate curvature, and joint interactions reinforce this mechanism (Appendix C.1). Section 6.3 also newly argues for applicability with scarce adaptation data.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies Hessian-vector products for computing curvature terms in Appendix C.1. Existing initialization grids, STE temperature, optimizer settings, hardware, and code/checkpoint sources remain unchanged. Computational-cost details moved from v2 Appendix C.2 into the main text are retained disclosures.

R1.justification: v3 adds Marczak et al. (2025) and positions Iso-CTS as another strong SVD-based merging comparator. The broader related-work discussion, novelty framing, and other cited works are retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains unchanged. v3 reorders analysis passages, moves the computational-cost discussion into Section 6.2, consolidates two algorithms into one listing, and updates affiliations, publication headers, and acknowledgements. The new scientific discussion is localized rather than a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 adds four analytical figures (6-9), two data-availability tables (7 and 10), and additional rows in the main comparison tables. It also relocates the unchanged cost table into the main text and reorganizes ablation and algorithm displays. All six original figure graphics are retained despite changed placement and numbering.

improvement.justification: The added Iso-CTS comparisons and matched AdaMerging language baselines make the empirical evaluation more complete, while Appendix C.1 provides useful additional mechanism analysis. However, the new data-efficiency tables contain unresolved inconsistencies with retained results (Tables 7 versus 1 and 10 versus 2), limiting confidence in that evidence. With the established method and results preserved, the net quality gain is modest.
